Re: Appeal of denial for partial knee replacement  
Member: Quinn Ellison  
Member ID: W391580594  
Reference number: POC-DF42BEB029-97975  
Requested procedure: Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446  
Date of denial notice: August 4, 2026

To Aetna Member Appeals:

I request reconsideration of Aetna’s denial of prior authorization for CPT 27446. The denial states that the submitted imaging does not support medical necessity. The submitted MRI directly documents advanced, isolated medial-compartment disease that supports the requested procedure under Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin 0660, Knee Arthroplasty.

Aetna’s policy states:

“Radiographic evidence of moderate/severe osteoarthritis (i.e., Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4) affecting only a single (medial, lateral or patellofemoral) compartment of the knee joint.”

The MRI performed on May 28, 2026, documents full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 disease medially. This is radiographic evidence of severe osteoarthritis affecting a single compartment, specifically the medial compartment. It directly addresses the imaging criterion cited above.

The clinical record also supports the other relevant medical-necessity factors in the policy:

- Progressive knee pain has continued for 18 months despite rest.
- The pain causes substantial functional impairment: I cannot climb stairs without assistance and awaken three to four times each night because of pain.
- Examination documented positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.
- I completed 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, including 24 visits from February 25, 2026, through June 17, 2026. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for eight months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 2, 2026, provided only four weeks of partial relief.
- BMI is 29, and there is no active infection, untreated substance use, or smoking history.

Aetna’s policy also states:

“Pain and functional disability that interferes with ADLs due to osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee joint.”

The documented inability to climb stairs without assistance and repeated nighttime awakenings demonstrate significant functional impairment. The policy further states:

“History of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management; 12 or 24 weeks depending on age/BMI) that is clearly addressed in the medical record ... with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy).”

The record documents 16 weeks and 24 visits of supervised, in-person physical therapy, along with eight months of unsuccessful NSAID treatment and only temporary, partial benefit from corticosteroid injection.

Please overturn the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 27446. If Aetna believes that any additional criterion remains unsatisfied, please identify that criterion specifically, provide the exact clinical review rationale, and identify every record or imaging finding relied upon in making that determination. Please also provide the version and date of the criteria applied to this request.

Enclosed are the supporting records:

1. MRI report dated May 28, 2026  
2. Physical therapy discharge note documenting treatment from February 25, 2026, through June 17, 2026  
3. Records documenting NSAID treatment and inadequate relief  
4. Record of corticosteroid injection dated May 2, 2026  
5. Orthopedic examination and clinical assessment by Lindqvist, MD

This appeal is submitted within the 180-day appeal period stated in the denial notice.

Sincerely,

Quinn Ellison
